content: Dr. Maarten has announced that his laboratory will receive a grant of $218,460 from the United States National Institutes of Health (NIH), specifically from the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID). This funding will support drug assays for a clinical trial investigating the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics (PK) of bedaquiline and delamanid, both as standalone treatments and in combination, for patients undergoing treatment for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB). This trial is part of the AIDS Clinical Trials Group study A5343. Dr. Maarten will not receive any salary support from this grant. The External Review Group (ERG) members listed below declared no conflicts of interest related to the objectives of the guidelines: Essam El Moghazi, Mildred Fernando-Pancho, Anna Marie Celina Garfin, Barend (Ben) Marais, Andrei Mary Andychev, Alberto Matteelli, Giovanni Battista Migliori, Nguyen Viet Nhung, Rohit Sarin, Welile Sikhondze, Ivan Solovic, Pedro Suarez, and Carlos Torres. Thato Mosidi, an ERG member, declared interests that were deemed not to conflict with the guidelines' objectives. She represents individuals affected by and living with tuberculosis (TB) on the Global Fund Country Coordinating Mechanism in South Africa. Additionally, she is an active member of TB Proof, a non-profit organization advocating for patient access to TB medications. Evidence reviewers from McGill University in Montreal, Canada—Syed Abidi, Jonathon Campbell, Zhiyi Lan, and Dick Menzies—declared no conflicts of interest with the guidelines' objectives. Faiz Ahmad Khan, another evidence reviewer, declared receiving payment from the World Health Organization (WHO) to collect data and conduct a meta-analysis on shorter MDR-TB regimens for the 2016 guidelines (CAD $4,080) and travel fees to present these findings at a Guideline Development Group (GDG) meeting in 2015. He also updated the same analysis from 2016 to 2018 for the American Thoracic Society (ATS) guidelines without receiving remuneration. The funding for the meetings and reviews involved in updating the 2011 guidelines for the programmatic management of drug-resistant tuberculosis came entirely from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID). Experts on the GDG and their affiliated institutions contributed their time to discussions and activities related to the update process. All non-WHO members of the GDG, ERG, and academic centers involved in the reviews completed Declaration of Interest forms. Four GDG members declared interests that were judged to represent potential conflicts and were excused from sessions during the October 25–27, 2010, meeting where drug regimen recommendations were discussed. Jaime Bayona served as a consultant for the development of clinical trial designs for studies on an anti-tuberculosis drug manufactured by Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd. (OPC-67683). Charles L. Daley chaired drug safety monitoring for two trials conducted by Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd. Carole D. Mitnick was a member of the Scientific Advisory Board of Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd. and advised on drug OPC-67683. Ma. Imelda Quelapio received monetary and non-monetary research support from Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd. The following academic center members who reviewed evidence for the guidelines presented their findings at the meeting: Matthew Arentz, Melissa Bauer, Richard Menzies, Carole D. Mitnick, Olivia Oxlade, Patricia Pavlinac, and Judd L. Walson. They did not participate in formulating recommendations related to their evidence reviews. The 2016 update of the WHO treatment guidelines for drug-resistant tuberculosis followed WHO's conflict of interest policy. All GDG members completed Declaration of Interest forms, which were reviewed by the WHO Guideline Steering Committee. GDG members with no conflicting interests included Luis Gustavo do Valle Bastos, José A. Caminero, Tsira Chakhaiya, Michel Gasana, Armen Hayrapetyan, Antonia Kwiecien, Sundari Mase, Nguyen Viet Nhung, Maria Rodriguez, Holger Schünemann, James Seddon, and Alena Skrahina. Farhana Amanullah declared receiving funding for consultancies and travel from WHO, as well as grants from the Global Fund and TB-REACH to cover her salary (10% full-time equivalent). Daniela Cirillo declared funding from FIND to evaluate drug susceptibility testing (DST) for new drugs and from Otsuka to evaluate DST for delamanid. She also heads a supranational TB reference laboratory in Italy and is a member of the Italian national committee for bedaquiline use. Charles L. Daley declared funding from Otsuka to chair the data monitoring committee for delamanid trials. Kelly Dooley declared funding to provide expert advice on trial design for TB/HIV and her roles as co-chair of the AIDS Clinical Trials Group (ACTG) study assessing bedaquiline and delamanid, principal investigator for a trial assessing pretomanid, and investigator in trials on high-dose isoniazid for MDR-TB, rifapentine for latent TB infection in pregnant women and children, and bedaquiline and delamanid for children with MDR-TB and HIV. Agnes Gebhard works for the KNCV TB Foundation, which has projects funded by the Eli Lilly and Company Foundation and collaborates with Cepheid on GeneXpert machine installations. Carlos Torres-Duque received honoraria from Janssen Pharmaceuticals for presentations on TB prevention and WHO policy on bedaquiline. Tom Shinnick, an employee of the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), served on the Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) for delamanid trials organized by Otsuka as part of his official CDC duties. He received no remuneration for this role, and CDC covered all related travel expenses. Lindsay McKenna declared non-commercial support to the Treatment Action Group (TAG) from various organizations, including the Stop TB Partnership and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. She was recused from discussions on MDR-TB regimen composition during the November 9, 2015, meeting. José A. Caminero, a staff consultant for the International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (UNION), was recused from discussions on shorter MDR-TB regimens during the November 10, 2015, meeting. The ERG members Chen-Yuan Chiang, Celine Garfin, Michael Kimerling, Vaira Leimane, Gao Mengqiu, Norbert Ndjeka, Ejaz Qadeer, Lee Reichman, Rohit Sarin, and Irina Vasilyeva declared no interests related to the meeting's objectives. Guy Marks declared research support from AERAS for evaluating latent TB infection and TB recurrence rates in Vietnam. He also serves as Vice-President of the UNION and Editor-in-Chief of the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease. Dalene von Delft declared receiving support from various organizations for travel and accommodation to give presentations on drug-resistant TB. She also received bedaquiline as part of her MDR-TB treatment through a compassionate use program in 2011. Evidence reviewers for the systematic reviews included Mayara Bastos, Gregory J. Fox, Faiz Ahmad Khan, and Richard (Dick) Menzies from McGill University; Katherine Fielding, Rebecca Harris, Mishal Khan, and David Moore from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine; and Anneke Hesseling from Stellenbosch University. They did not participate in formulating policy recommendations. Gregory J. Fox declared receiving support from the UNION to attend the 2015 International UNION Conference and receive the Young Innovator Award. Katherine Fielding declared her employer received funding from Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) for statistical support for the TB-PRACTECAL study. Rebecca Harris declared consulting for a clinical research organization working for GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) vaccines. David Moore declared research support from the Wellcome Trust Research Training Fellowship Programme. Anneke Hesseling declared her employer received funding from Otsuka Pharmaceutical for her work on delamanid clinical trials in children.
